title: Named means joined?
hook: Does a conditional mention in the Act prove a colony actually joined?

doesNotKnow: Distinguish New Zealand’s conditional mention in an Act from the six colonies actually named in the 1900 proclamation.

claims.text: Conditional mention differs from the proclamation’s membership for 1 January 1901. These are UK parliamentary and Crown records of colonial units, not peoples. They establish neither Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander or Māori hapū/iwi assent, extinguished institutions nor Sydney and Wellington’s whole history. Matike Mai’s 2016 account interprets the 1840 Tiriti relationship as iwi/hapū rangatiratanga authority, Crown kāwanatanga governance and joint decisions. This working-group interpretation is not unanimous assent or a Crown ruling; a colonial membership list cannot supply that agreement relationship.
